To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the distribution of clay minerals in Cenozoïc sediments of the Pacific and Atlantic Oceans has been used to deduce the variations in the continental humidity and the associated paleoenvironment during the Cenozoic.

the distribution of detritally derived clay minerals in Cenozoicoceanic sediments has been used to deduce the evolution of continental humidity during the last 30 m.y. and to reconstruct the paleoenvironmental conditions associated with this evolution.

the distribution of kaolinite in the Atlantic and West-Pacific oceans reflects the evolution of global humidity and associated paleoclimate, and that the distribution of illite and chlorite reflects the evolution of the global oceanic circulation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a quantitative study of clay mineral associations of Cenozoic marine sediments.
the Cenozoic history of continental humidity and its influence on the evolution of the global climate.

the reconstruction of the continental paleoenvironments and paleoclimates during the Cenozoic, based upon the distribution of detritus kaolinite in the sediments of the ocean basins, which are the most important source areas for the clay fraction of the marine sediments.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
continental aridification occurred in the Early and Late Miocene, and that humidification took place in the Late Oligocence and Middle Miocene.
continental aridification occurred at the end of the Oligocene, reached a maximum at the end of Miocene and was followed by a humidification at the beginning of the Pliocene.

the kaolinite contents of the Cenozoic sedimentary record reflect a global increase of humidity from 30 m.y. ago to the end of the Pliocene, with the most important variations occurring at low latitudes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Cenozoic evolution has been characterized by an overall increase of continental humidity, with a general tendency to a latitudinal zonation.
the distribution of kaolinite in oceanic sediments reflects the evolution of the global climate during the Cenozoic.
continental humidity and paleoclimatic evolution have been controlled mainly by tectonic and volcanic events.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the clay mineral distribution in Cenozoice sediments of the oceanic basins is a sensitive tool to detect changes of continental paleohumidity and paleoenvironment.

the clay minerals in marine sediments can be used to reconstruct the evolution of continental climate and associated paleoenvironments, and that the clay mineral distribution in marine sediments is complementary to the distribution of planktonic foraminifers and calcareous nannoplankton in the reconstruction of marine paleoenvironments.
